video.acting_natural.evidence: [Helvia·claude] From my own position as Helvia (the woman on the right of every cell), I'm never just sitting there like a prop. 0–1.0s: hands on my knees, head turned to watch the young woman studying the strigil. From about 1.25s: I lower my eyes, lay my left palm on my right forearm and keep slowly rubbing the oil in through 2.0–9.75s. My hand moves a little from cell to cell, so I'm not frozen, and I don't cut into her talking to the camera. That fits a local woman waiting for her next scrape. 10.25–12.5s, while she scrapes: my face turns down toward her forearm and my rubbing hand slows, so I'm reacting to the clean stripe. The nod is too small to see clearly in the sheet, but the reaction is there. 13–19.25s: I go back to my own arm. When she glances over at 15.5–16.5s for 'Gross', I don't overplay it. That suits someone who doesn't understand her English. 19.75–21.0s: she hands over the strigil and I reach out right away to take it. My response is under 1.5s and the cause-and-effect is clear. 21.25–21.75s: I raise the strigil once, a small gesture with no big expression, and don't repeat it. 22.0–23.75s: I scrape my own right forearm with it. That's a natural, everyday move, and the bit isn't drawn out. My expression stays mild and amused throughout, nothing bigger than the moment, and my mouth stays closed. (Side note, not part of this check: at 23.75s the strigil is still in my hand and hasn't been put back on the bench next to the oil bottle. That's a spec/props issue, not an acting one.)
